claim: UCoder uses execution-signature consensus clustering over n=128 densely sampled candidate solutions -- an expensive many-sample self-consistency signal, not a cheap single-pass probe -- as its primary correctness proxy for unsupervised self-training.
stance_target: expensive repeated-sampling remains the most reliable internal correctness signal in current practice, reinforcing the base paper's premise that a cheap equivalent does not yet exist
scope_conditions: self-generated programming problems, Qwen2.5-Coder base models 7B/14B/32B
quoted_support: we probe the solution space via dense sampling, where execution-driven consensus clustering reveals that correct implementations form tight clusters while incorrect ones are dispersed.

claim: Consensus Convergence theorem formally guarantees that the largest execution-signature cluster among n sampled candidates is entirely correct with probability >= 1-delta-n^2*p^|T|, given sufficient test-set size |T| >= log(n/k)/(-log p), providing theoretical grounding for sampling-based correctness estimation.
stance_target: sampling-based correctness signals have formal statistical guarantees that single-pass probes currently lack
scope_conditions: candidates independently sampled from a model; incorrect implementations assumed to disagree with probability >= 1-p per test
quoted_support: If the test set size satisfies |T| >= log(n/k)/(-log p), then the largest consensus cluster C_max contains only correct implementations with probability at least P(C_max is correct) >= 1-delta-n^2 p^|T|.

claim: Perplexity (fluency), a free log-prob-derived signal computed from the already-generated token probabilities, correlates with execution success but only weakly/coarsely: solutions with execution success rate above 80% cluster below perplexity 1.05, with rapid degradation beyond that threshold, over 9,700 sampled candidates.
stance_target: log-prob-based signals (a form of expressed/interpretable confidence) carry some correctness information but are used only as a secondary tie-breaker, not a primary correctness detector
quoted_support: solutions with execution success rates above 80% cluster predominantly below perplexity 1.05, with rapid performance degradation beyond this range.

claim: UCoder-7B trained with zero external labeled data matches or beats the fully supervised Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on several benchmarks (BigCodeBench-Complete, BigCodeBench-Instruct, FullStackBench) despite using no human-annotated instructions.
stance_target: background context on unsupervised code-LLM training using self-consistency signals -- tangential to the interface/calibration question but confirms the value of sampling-derived training signal
scope_conditions: HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), BigCodeBench, LiveCodeBench, FullStackBench, single 7B-32B model scales
quoted_support: Despite using no external data, UCoder achieves comparable performance to the supervised baseline across multiple benchmarks.
